title: BIST-OUCH: Add orderbook tracking feature

How long will these update chains get?  If you are using large captures, and this linear search (on later passes) becomes too slow, you might consider changing the data to instead be a map looked up by frame number, or attached per-packet info to frame, or populate a separate result table to be written on first pass and looked after.
OrderChain length doesn’t affect per-packet time; memory is O(#msgs + #unique tokens). If you mean something else, I can answer that.
Every time you call ob_find_root(), you are walking a linked list - how many times might an order get updated?  You had a screenshot where an order chain reached index number 19 at least..
Actually, I tried to decode as step as I can do much, it worked in every try, I can't remember now, but I remember it had more than 2000+ order chains in that .pcap file.

I think the order chains themselves are looked by in a map/table, so having a large number of those should be ok if your key/hash is good.  But if an order chain has seen lots of replacements, you might end up doing lots of linear walks to reach the root.  You could of course just store the root separately, and I may have misunderstood what you are doing from only a quick reading.

I won't have time to have a deeper look today, hopefully tomorrow.
